sections.narration_script: Start-Up. Look outside the window! Is it sunny, cloudy, or rainy? Have you ever noticed how the weather changes throughout the day? Some places are always warm, while others are cold. Why does this happen? In this chapter, we will explore the differences between weather and climate and understand the factors that influence them.

sections.description: Distinct hot dry dunes and warm rainy rainforest shots, timed to Sahara and Amazon descriptions; authored 30-year comparison graphic.
sections.narration_script: Climate. Climate is the average weather condition of a place over a long period, usually 30 years or more. It tells us whether a place is generally hot, cold, wet, or dry. For example, the climate of the Sahara Desert is hot and dry, while the climate of the Amazon Rainforest is warm and rainy.

sections.title: Distance from the Equator (Latitudes)
sections.description: A new blue 3D globe with authored latitude rings and sunlight paths toward the equator and poles; original textbook world map shown unchanged.
sections.narration_script: Distance from the Equator (Latitudes). The Earth is divided into imaginary lines called latitudes. Places near the equator receive direct sunlight throughout the year, making them hot. As we move towards the poles, sunlight spreads out, making these areas cooler. This is why tropical regions are warm, while polar regions are cold.

sections.title: Distance from the Sea (Sea Breeze and Land Breeze)
sections.description: Precise coastal 3D model with day sea-to-land airflow and night land-to-sea airflow; preserve the original two-panel breeze diagram.
sections.narration_script: Distance from the Sea (Sea Breeze and Land Breeze). Oceans and seas influence the climate of coastal areas. Water heats up and cools down more slowly than land. During the day, land heats up faster than water, causing a sea breeze to blow from the sea to the land. At night, the land cools down quickly, and a land breeze blows from land to the sea. This keeps coastal areas cooler in summer and warmer in winter compared to inland regions.

sections.title: Let's Remember
sections.description: Exact five-item Let’s Remember list on a cream reading panel with word-highlight subtitles.
sections.narration_script: Let's Remember. Weather is the daily atmospheric condition of a place. Climate is the average weather over a long period. Latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, and winds influence climate. The world has different types of climate, including tropical, desert, and tundra. The Earth has three climatic zones: torrid, temperate, and frigid.
